NKJV.1: Moreover he made a bronze altar: twenty cubits was its length, twenty cubits its width, and ten cubits its height.
NKJV.2: Then he made the Sea of cast bronze, ten cubits from one brim to the other; it was completely round. Its height was five cubits, and a line of thirty cubits measured its circumference.
NKJV.3: And under it was the likeness of oxen encircling it all around, ten to a cubit, all the way around the Sea. The oxen were cast in two rows, when it was cast.
NKJV.4: It stood on twelve oxen: three looking toward the north, three looking toward the west, three looking toward the south, and three looking toward the east; the Sea was set upon them, and all their back parts pointed inward.
NKJV.5: It was a handbreadth thick; and its brim was shaped like the brim of a cup, like a lily blossom. It contained three thousand baths.
NKJV.6: He also made ten lavers, and put five on the right side and five on the left, to wash in them; such things as they offered for the burnt offering they would wash in them, but the Sea was for the priests to wash in.
NKJV.7: And he made ten lampstands of gold according to their design, and set them in the temple, five on the right side and five on the left.
NKJV.8: He also made ten tables, and placed them in the temple, five on the right side and five on the left. And he made one hundred bowls of gold.
NKJV.9: Furthermore he made the court of the priests, and the great court and doors for the court; and he overlaid these doors with bronze.
NKJV.10: He set the Sea on the right side, toward the southeast.
NKJV.11: Then Huram made the pots and the shovels and the bowls. So Huram finished doing the work that he was to do for King Solomon for the house of God:
NKJV.12: the two pillars and the bowl-shaped capitals that were on top of the two pillars; the two networks covering the two bowl-shaped capitals which were on top of the pillars;
NKJV.13: four hundred pomegranates for the two networks (two rows of pomegranates for each network, to cover the two bowl-shaped capitals that were on the pillars);
NKJV.14: he also made carts and the lavers on the carts;
NKJV.15: one Sea and twelve oxen under it;
NKJV.16: also the pots, the shovels, the forks—and all their articles Huram his master craftsman made of burnished bronze for King Solomon for the house of the LORD.
NKJV.17: In the plain of Jordan the king had them cast in clay molds, between Succoth and Zeredah.
NKJV.18: And Solomon had all these articles made in such great abundance that the weight of the bronze was not determined.
NKJV.19: Thus Solomon had all the furnishings made for the house of God: the altar of gold and the tables on which was the showbread;
NKJV.20: the lampstands with their lamps of pure gold, to burn in the prescribed manner in front of the inner sanctuary,
NKJV.21: with the flowers and the lamps and the wick-trimmers of gold, of purest gold;
NKJV.22: the trimmers, the bowls, the ladles, and the censers of pure gold. As for the entry of the sanctuary, its inner doors to the Most Holy Place, and the doors of the main hall of the temple, were gold.

ESV.1: He made an altar of bronze, twenty cubits  long and twenty cubits wide and ten cubits high.
ESV.2: Then he made the sea of cast metal. It was round, ten cubits from brim to brim, and five cubits high, and a line of thirty cubits measured its circumference.
ESV.3: Under it were figures of gourds,  for ten cubits, compassing the sea all around. The gourds were in two rows, cast with it when it was cast.
ESV.4: It stood on twelve oxen, three facing north, three facing west, three facing south, and three facing east. The sea was set on them, and all their rear parts were inward.
ESV.5: Its thickness was a handbreadth.  And its brim was made like the brim of a cup, like the flower of a lily. It held 3,000 baths.
ESV.6: He also made ten basins in which to wash, and set five on the south side, and five on the north side. In these they were to rinse off what was used for the burnt offering, and the sea was for the priests to wash in.
ESV.7: And he made ten golden lampstands as prescribed, and set them in the temple, five on the south side and five on the north.
ESV.8: He also made ten tables and placed them in the temple, five on the south side and five on the north. And he made a hundred basins of gold.
ESV.9: He made the court of the priests and the great court and doors for the court and overlaid their doors with bronze.
ESV.10: And he set the sea at the southeast corner of the house.
ESV.11: Hiram also made the pots, the shovels, and the basins. So Hiram finished the work that he did for King Solomon on the house of God:
ESV.12: the two pillars, the bowls, and the two capitals on the top of the pillars; and the two latticeworks to cover the two bowls of the capitals that were on the top of the pillars;
ESV.13: and the 400 pomegranates for the two latticeworks, two rows of pomegranates for each latticework, to cover the two bowls of the capitals that were on the pillars.
ESV.14: He made the stands also, and the basins on the stands,
ESV.15: and the one sea, and the twelve oxen underneath it.
ESV.16: The pots, the shovels, the forks, and all the equipment for these  Huram-abi made of burnished bronze for King Solomon for the house of the LORD.
ESV.17: In the plain of the Jordan the king cast them, in the clay ground between Succoth and Zeredah.
ESV.18: Solomon made all these things in great quantities, for the weight of the bronze was not sought.
ESV.19: So Solomon made all the vessels that were in the house of God: the golden altar, the tables for the bread of the Presence,
ESV.20: the lampstands and their lamps of pure gold to burn before the inner sanctuary, as prescribed;
ESV.21: the flowers, the lamps, and the tongs, of purest gold;
ESV.22: the snuffers, basins, dishes for incense, and fire pans, of pure gold, and the sockets  of the temple, for the inner doors to the Most Holy Place and for the doors of the nave of the temple were of gold.

NASB.1: Then he made a bronze altar, twenty cubits in length and twenty cubits in width and ten cubits in height.
NASB.2: Also he made the cast [metal] sea, ten cubits from brim to brim, circular in form, and its height [was] five cubits and its circumference thirty cubits.
NASB.3: Now figures like oxen [were] under it [and] all around it, ten cubits, entirely encircling the sea. The oxen [were] in two rows, cast in one piece.
NASB.4: It stood on twelve oxen, three facing the north, three facing west, three facing south and three facing east; and the sea [was set] on top of them and all their hindquarters turned inwards.
NASB.5: It was a handbreadth thick, and its brim was made like the brim of a cup, [like] a lily blossom; it could hold 3,000 baths.
NASB.6: He also made ten basins in which to wash, and he set five on the right side and five on the left to rinse things for the burnt offering; but the sea [was] for the priests to wash in.
NASB.7: Then he made the ten golden lampstands in the way prescribed for them and he set them in the temple, five on the right side and five on the left.
NASB.8: He also made ten tables and placed them in the temple, five on the right side and five on the left. And he made one hundred golden bowls.
NASB.9: Then he made the court of the priests and the great court and doors for the court, and overlaid their doors with bronze.
NASB.10: He set the sea on the right side [of the house] toward the southeast.
NASB.11: Huram also made the pails, the shovels and the bowls. So Huram finished doing the work which he performed for King Solomon in the house of God:
NASB.12: the two pillars, the bowls and the two capitals on top of the pillars, and the two networks to cover the two bowls of the capitals which were on top of the pillars,
NASB.13: and the four hundred pomegranates for the two networks, two rows of pomegranates for each network to cover the two bowls of the capitals which were on the pillars.
NASB.14: He also made the stands and he made the basins on the stands,
NASB.15: [and] the one sea with the twelve oxen under it.
NASB.16: The pails, the shovels, the forks and all its utensils, Huram-abi made of polished bronze for King Solomon for the house of the LORD.
NASB.17: On the plain of the Jordan the king cast them in the clay ground between Succoth and Zeredah.
NASB.18: Thus Solomon made all these utensils in great quantities, for the weight of the bronze could not be found out.
NASB.19: Solomon also made all the things that [were] in the house of God: even the golden altar, the tables with the bread of the Presence on them,
NASB.20: the lampstands with their lamps of pure gold, to burn in front of the inner sanctuary in the way prescribed;
NASB.21: the flowers, the lamps, and the tongs of gold, of purest gold;
NASB.22: and the snuffers, the bowls, the spoons and the firepans of pure gold; and the entrance of the house, its inner doors for the holy of holies and the doors of the house, [that is], of the nave, of gold.

WEB.1: Then he made an altar of brass, twenty cubits  long, twenty cubits wide, and ten cubits high.
WEB.2: Also he made the molten sea  of ten cubits from brim to brim. It was round, five cubits high, and thirty cubits in circumference.
WEB.3: Under it was the likeness of oxen, which encircled it, for ten cubits, encircling the sea. The oxen were in two rows, cast when it was cast.
WEB.4: It stood on twelve oxen, three looking toward the north, and three looking toward the west, and three looking toward the south, and three looking toward the east; and the sea was set on them above, and all their hindquarters were inward.
WEB.5: It was a handbreadth thick; and its brim was made like the brim of a cup, like the flower of a lily. It received and held three thousand baths.
WEB.6: He also made ten basins, and put five on the right hand, and five on the left, to wash in them. The things that belonged to the burnt offering were washed in them; but the sea was for the priests to wash in.
WEB.7: He made the ten lamp stands of gold according to the ordinance concerning them; and he set them in the temple, five on the right hand, and five on the left.
WEB.8: He made also ten tables, and placed them in the temple, five on the right side, and five on the left. He made one hundred basins of gold.
WEB.9: Furthermore he made the court of the priests, the great court, and doors for the court, and overlaid their doors with brass.
WEB.10: He set the sea on the right side of the house eastward, toward the south.
WEB.11: Huram made the pots, the shovels, and the basins. So Huram finished doing the work that he did for king Solomon in God’s house:
WEB.12: the two pillars, the bowls, the two capitals which were on the top of the pillars, the two networks to cover the two bowls of the capitals that were on the top of the pillars,
WEB.13: and the four hundred pomegranates for the two networks; two rows of pomegranates for each network, to cover the two bowls of the capitals that were on the pillars.
WEB.14: He also made the bases, and he made the basins on the bases;
WEB.15: one sea, and the twelve oxen under it.
WEB.16: Huram his father also made the pots, the shovels, the forks, and all its vessels for king Solomon, for Yahweh’s house, of bright brass.
WEB.17: The king cast them in the plain of the Jordan, in the clay ground between Succoth and Zeredah.
WEB.18: Thus Solomon made all these vessels in great abundance; for the weight of the brass could not be determined.
WEB.19: Solomon made all the vessels that were in God’s house, the golden altar also, and the tables with the show bread on them;
WEB.20: and the lamp stands with their lamps, to burn according to the ordinance before the inner sanctuary, of pure gold;
WEB.21: and the flowers, the lamps, and the tongs of gold that was perfect gold;
WEB.22: and the snuffers, the basins, the spoons, and the fire pans of pure gold. As for the entry of the house, its inner doors for the most holy place and the doors of the main hall of the temple were of gold.

AMP.1: Then Solomon made an altar of bronze, twenty cubits in length, twenty cubits in width, and ten cubits in height.
AMP.2: He also made the Sea [that is, the large basin used for ceremonial washing] of cast metal, ten cubits from brim to brim, circular in form, and five cubits in height, and its circumference was thirty cubits.
AMP.3: Under it and entirely encircling it were figures of oxen, ten to a cubit. The oxen were in two rows, cast in one piece.
AMP.4: It stood on twelve oxen, three facing north, three facing west, three facing south, three facing east; and the Sea was set on top of them and all their hindquarters turned inward.
AMP.5: It was a handbreadth (the width of the four fingers) thick; its brim was made like the brim of a cup, like a lily blossom. It could hold3,000 baths (measures).
AMP.6: He also made ten [portable] basins in which to wash, and he put five on the right (south) side and five on the left (north). They would rinse things for the burnt offering in them, but the Sea was for the priests to wash in.
AMP.7: And he made ten golden lampstands just as directed and set them in the temple, five on the right side and five on the left.
AMP.8: He made also ten tables and placed them in the temple, five on the right side and five on the left side, and he made a hundred [ceremonial] basins of gold.
AMP.9: Moreover, he made the courtyard of the priests, and the great courtyard [for the people] and doors for the courtyard, and he overlaid their doors with bronze.
AMP.10: He set the Sea on the right side at the southeast corner [of the house].
AMP.11: And Huram also made the pails [for ashes], the shovels, and the basins. So Huram finished the work that he did for King Solomon in the house of God:
AMP.12: the two pillars, the bowls, the capitals on top of the two pillars, and the two lattice works to cover the two bowls of the capitals which were on top of the pillars,
AMP.13: and the four hundred pomegranates for the two lattice works, two rows of pomegranates for each lattice to cover the two bowls of the capitals on the pillars.
AMP.14: He also made the stands and he made the basins on the stands;
AMP.15: and the one Sea with the twelve oxen under it.
AMP.16: The pails, the shovels, and the meat-forks, and all the utensils Huram-abi made of polished bronze for King Solomon for the house of the LORD.
AMP.17: The king cast them on the plain of the Jordan, in the clay ground between Succoth and Zeredah.
AMP.18: Solomon made all these utensils in such great quantity that the weight of the bronze could not be determined.
AMP.19: Solomon also made all the articles that were in the house of God: the golden altar, and the tables for the bread of the Presence (showbread),
AMP.20: and the lampstands with their lamps of pure gold, to burn in front of the inner sanctuary (the Holy of Holies) as directed;
AMP.21: the flowers, the lamps, and the tongs of gold, of purest gold;
AMP.22: and the snuffers, the basins, the dishes [for incense], and the firepans, of pure gold; and for the entrance of the house (temple), the inner doors for the Holy of Holies and the doors of the Holy Place (main room), were of gold.

NLT.1: Solomon also made a bronze altar 30 feet long, 30 feet wide, and 15 feet high.
NLT.2: Then he cast a great round basin, 15 feet across from rim to rim, called the Sea. It was 7 1⁄2 feet deep and about 45 feet in circumference.
NLT.3: It was encircled just below its rim by two rows of figures that resembled oxen. There were about six oxen per foot all the way around, and they were cast as part of the basin.
NLT.4: The Sea was placed on a base of twelve bronze oxen, all facing outward. Three faced north, three faced west, three faced south, and three faced east, and the Sea rested on them.
NLT.5: The walls of the Sea were about three inches thick, and its rim flared out like a cup and resembled a water lily blossom. It could hold about 16,500 gallons of water.
NLT.6: He also made ten smaller basins for washing the utensils for the burnt offerings. He set five on the south side and five on the north. But the priests washed themselves in the Sea.
NLT.7: He then cast ten gold lampstands according to the specifications that had been given, and he put them in the Temple. Five were placed against the south wall, and five were placed against the north wall.
NLT.8: He also built ten tables and placed them in the Temple, five along the south wall and five along the north wall. Then he molded 100 gold basins.
NLT.9: He then built a courtyard for the priests, and also the large outer courtyard. He made doors for the courtyard entrances and overlaid them with bronze.
NLT.10: The great bronze basin called the Sea was placed near the southeast corner of the Temple.
NLT.11: Huram-abi also made the necessary washbasins, shovels, and bowls. So at last Huram-abi completed everything King Solomon had assigned him to make for the Temple of God:
NLT.12:
the two pillars;
the two bowl-shaped capitals on top of the pillars;
the two networks of interwoven chains that decorated the capitals;
NLT.13: the 400 pomegranates that hung from the chains on the capitals (two rows of pomegranates for each of the chain networks that decorated the capitals on top of the pillars);
NLT.14: the water carts holding the basins;
NLT.15: the Sea and the twelve oxen under it;
NLT.16:
the ash buckets, the shovels, the meat hooks, and all the related articles.
Huram-abi made all these things of burnished bronze for the Temple of the LORD, just as King Solomon had directed.
NLT.17: The king had them cast in clay molds in the Jordan Valley between Succoth and Zarethan.
NLT.18: Solomon used such great quantities of bronze that its weight could not be determined.
NLT.19:
Solomon also made all the furnishings for the Temple of God: the gold altar;
the tables for the Bread of the Presence;
NLT.20: the lampstands and their lamps of solid gold, to burn in front of the Most Holy Place as prescribed;
NLT.21: the flower decorations, lamps, and tongs — all of the purest gold;
NLT.22:
the lamp snuffers, bowls, ladles, and incense burners — all of solid gold;
the doors for the entrances to the Most Holy Place and the main room of the Temple, overlaid with gold.

CSB17.1: He made a bronze altar <sup>ⓐ</sup> 30 feet <sup>[1]</sup> long, 30 feet wide, and 15 feet <sup>[2]</sup> high.
CSB17.2: Then he made the cast metal basin, <sup>[3]</sup> <sup>ⓑ</sup> 15 feet from brim to brim, perfectly round. It was 7½ feet <sup>[4]</sup> high and 45 feet <sup>[5]</sup> in circumference.
CSB17.3: The likeness of oxen <sup>[6]</sup> was below it, completely encircling it, ten every half yard, <sup>[7]</sup> completely surrounding the basin. The oxen were cast in two rows when the basin was cast.
CSB17.4: It stood on twelve oxen, three facing north, three facing west, three facing south, and three facing east. The basin was on top of them and all their hindquarters were toward the center.
CSB17.5: The basin was three inches <sup>[8]</sup> thick, and its rim was fashioned like the brim of a cup or a lily blossom. It could hold eleven thousand gallons. <sup>[9]</sup>
CSB17.6: He made ten basins for washing and he put five on the right and five on the left. <sup>ⓒ</sup> The parts of the burnt offering were rinsed in them, <sup>ⓓ</sup> but the basin was used by the priests for washing.
CSB17.7: He made the ten gold lampstands according to their specifications and put them in the sanctuary, five on the right and five on the left. <sup>ⓔ</sup>
CSB17.8: He made ten tables and placed them in the sanctuary, five on the right and five on the left. <sup>ⓕ</sup> He also made a hundred gold bowls.
CSB17.9: He made the courtyard <sup>ⓖ</sup> of the priests and the large court, and doors for the court. He overlaid the doors with bronze.
CSB17.10: He put the basin on the right side, toward the southeast. <sup>ⓗ</sup>
CSB17.11: Then Huram <sup>[10]</sup> <sup>ⓘ</sup> made <sup>ⓙ</sup> the pots, the shovels, and the bowls. So Huram finished doing the work that he was doing for King Solomon in God’s temple:
CSB17.12: two pillars; the bowls and the capitals on top of the two pillars; the two gratings for covering both bowls of the capitals that were on top of the pillars;
CSB17.13: the four hundred pomegranates for the two gratings (two rows of pomegranates for each grating covering both capitals’ bowls on top of the pillars <sup>ⓚ</sup>).
CSB17.14: He also made the water carts <sup>[11]</sup> <sup>ⓛ</sup> and the basins on the water carts.
CSB17.15: The one basin and the twelve oxen underneath it,
CSB17.16: the pots, the shovels, the forks, and all their utensils — Huram-abi <sup>[12]</sup> <sup>ⓜ</sup> made them for King Solomon for the LORD’s temple. All these were made of polished bronze.
CSB17.17: The king had them cast in clay molds in the Jordan Valley between Succoth and Zeredah.
CSB17.18: Solomon made all these utensils in such great abundance that the weight of the bronze was not determined.
CSB17.19: Solomon also made all the equipment in God’s temple: the gold altar; the tables on which to put the Bread of the Presence; <sup>ⓝ</sup>
CSB17.20: the lampstands and their lamps of pure gold to burn in front of the inner sanctuary according to specifications; <sup>ⓐ</sup>
CSB17.21: the flowers, lamps, and gold tongs — of purest gold;
CSB17.22: the wick trimmers, sprinkling basins, ladles, <sup>[13]</sup> and firepans — of purest gold; and the entryway to the temple, its inner doors to the most holy place, and the doors of the temple sanctuary — of gold.

NRSVCE.1: He made an altar of bronze, twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and ten cubits high.
NRSVCE.2: Then he made the molten sea; it was round, ten cubits from rim to rim, and five cubits high. A line of thirty cubits would encircle it completely.
NRSVCE.3: Under it were panels all around, each of ten cubits, surrounding the sea; there were two rows of panels, cast when it was cast.
NRSVCE.4: It stood on twelve oxen, three facing north, three facing west, three facing south, and three facing east; the sea was set on them. The hindquarters of each were toward the inside.
NRSVCE.5: Its thickness was a handbreadth; its rim was made like the rim of a cup, like the flower of a lily; it held three thousand baths.
NRSVCE.6: He also made ten basins in which to wash, and set five on the right side, and five on the left. In these they were to rinse what was used for the burnt offering. The sea was for the priests to wash in.
NRSVCE.7: He made ten golden lampstands as prescribed, and set them in the temple, five on the south side and five on the north.
NRSVCE.8: He also made ten tables and placed them in the temple, five on the right side and five on the left. And he made one hundred basins of gold.
NRSVCE.9: He made the court of the priests, and the great court, and doors for the court; he overlaid their doors with bronze.
NRSVCE.10: He set the sea at the southeast corner of the house.
NRSVCE.11: And Huram made the pots, the shovels, and the basins. Thus Huram finished the work that he did for King Solomon on the house of God:
NRSVCE.12: the two pillars, the bowls, and the two capitals on the top of the pillars; and the two latticeworks to cover the two bowls of the capitals that were on the top of the pillars;
NRSVCE.13: the four hundred pomegranates for the two latticeworks, two rows of pomegranates for each latticework, to cover the two bowls of the capitals that were on the pillars.
NRSVCE.14: He made the stands, the basins on the stands,
NRSVCE.15: the one sea, and the twelve oxen underneath it.
NRSVCE.16: The pots, the shovels, the forks, and all the equipment for these Huram-abi made of burnished bronze for King Solomon for the house of the LORD.
NRSVCE.17: In the plain of the Jordan the king cast them, in the clay ground between Succoth and Zeredah.
NRSVCE.18: Solomon made all these things in great quantities, so that the weight of the bronze was not determined.
NRSVCE.19: So Solomon made all the things that were in the house of God: the golden altar, the tables for the bread of the Presence,
NRSVCE.20: the lampstands and their lamps of pure gold to burn before the inner sanctuary, as prescribed;
NRSVCE.21: the flowers, the lamps, and the tongs, of purest gold;
NRSVCE.22: the snuffers, basins, ladles, and firepans, of pure gold. As for the entrance to the temple: the inner doors to the most holy place and the doors of the nave of the temple were of gold.

NET.1: He made a bronze altar, 30 feet long, 30 feet wide, and 15 feet high.
NET.2: He also made the big bronze basin called “The Sea.” It measured 15 feet from rim to rim, was circular in shape, and stood seven and one-half feet high. Its circumference was 45 feet.
NET.3: Images of bulls were under it all the way around, ten every eighteen inches all the way around. The bulls were in two rows and had been cast with “The Sea.”
NET.4: “The Sea” stood on top of twelve bulls. Three faced northward, three westward, three southward, and three eastward. “The Sea” was placed on top of them, and they all faced outward.
NET.5: It was four fingers thick and its rim was like that of a cup shaped like a lily blossom. It could hold 18,000 gallons.
NET.6: He made ten washing basins; he put five on the south side and five on the north side. In them they rinsed the items used for burnt sacrifices; the priests washed in “The Sea.”
NET.7: He made ten gold lampstands according to specifications and put them in the temple, five on the right and five on the left.
NET.8: He made ten tables and set them in the temple, five on the right and five on the left. He also made one hundred gold bowls.
NET.9: He made the courtyard of the priests and the large enclosure and its doors; he plated their doors with bronze.
NET.10: He put “The Sea” on the south side, in the southeast corner.
NET.11: Huram Abi made the pots, shovels, and bowls. He finished all the work on God’s temple he had been assigned by King Solomon.
NET.12: He made the two pillars, the two bowl-shaped tops of the pillars, the latticework for the bowl-shaped tops of the two pillars,
NET.13: the four hundred pomegranate-shaped ornaments for the latticework of the two pillars (each latticework had two rows of these ornaments at the bowl-shaped top of the pillar),
NET.14: the ten movable stands with their ten basins,
NET.15: the big bronze basin called “The Sea” with its twelve bulls underneath,
NET.16: and the pots, shovels, and meat forks. All the items King Solomon assigned Huram Abi to make for the LORD’s temple were made from polished bronze.
NET.17: The king had them cast in earthen foundries in the region of the Jordan between Succoth and Zarethan.
NET.18: Solomon made so many of these items they did not weigh the bronze.
NET.19: Solomon also made these items for God’s temple: the gold altar, the tables on which the Bread of the Presence was kept,
NET.20: the pure gold lampstands and their lamps which burned as specified at the entrance to the inner sanctuary,
NET.21: the pure gold flower-shaped ornaments, lamps, and tongs,
NET.22: the pure gold trimming shears, basins, pans, and censers, and the gold door sockets for the inner sanctuary (the most holy place) and for the doors of the main hall of the temple.

NIV.1:
The Temple’s Furnishings
He made a bronze altar twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide and ten cubits high.
NIV.2: He made the Sea of cast metal, circular in shape, measuring ten cubits from rim to rim and five cubits high. It took a line of thirty cubits to measure around it.
NIV.3: Below the rim, figures of bulls encircled it—ten to a cubit. The bulls were cast in two rows in one piece with the Sea.
NIV.4: The Sea stood on twelve bulls, three facing north, three facing west, three facing south and three facing east. The Sea rested on top of them, and their hindquarters were toward the center.
NIV.5: It was a handbreadth in thickness, and its rim was like the rim of a cup, like a lily blossom. It held three thousand baths.
NIV.6: He then made ten basins for washing and placed five on the south side and five on the north. In them the things to be used for the burnt offerings were rinsed, but the Sea was to be used by the priests for washing.
NIV.7: He made ten gold lampstands according to the specifications for them and placed them in the temple, five on the south side and five on the north.
NIV.8: He made ten tables and placed them in the temple, five on the south side and five on the north. He also made a hundred gold sprinkling bowls.
NIV.9: He made the courtyard of the priests, and the large court and the doors for the court, and overlaid the doors with bronze.
NIV.10: He placed the Sea on the south side, at the southeast corner.
NIV.11:
He also made the pots and shovels and sprinkling bowls.
So Huram finished the work he had undertaken for King Solomon in the temple of God:
NIV.12:
the two pillars;
the two bowl-shaped capitals on top of the pillars;
the two sets of network decorating the two bowl-shaped capitals on top of the pillars;
NIV.13: the four hundred pomegranates for the two sets of network (two rows of pomegranates for each network, decorating the bowl-shaped capitals on top of the pillars);
NIV.15: the Sea and the twelve bulls under it;
NIV.16:
the pots, shovels, meat forks and all related articles.
All the objects that Huram-Abi made for King Solomon for the temple of the Lord were of polished bronze.
NIV.17: The king had them cast in clay molds in the plain of the Jordan between Succoth and Zarethan.
NIV.18: All these things that Solomon made amounted to so much that the weight of the bronze was not determined.
NIV.19:
Solomon also made all the furnishings that were in God’s temple:
the golden altar;
the tables on which was the bread of the Presence;
NIV.20: the lampstands of pure gold with their lamps, to burn in front of the inner sanctuary as prescribed;
NIV.21: the gold floral work and lamps and tongs (they were solid gold);
NIV.22: the pure gold wick trimmers, sprinkling bowls, dishes and censers; and the gold doors of the temple: the inner doors to the Most Holy Place and the doors of the main hall.

MSG.1: He made the Bronze Altar thirty feet long, thirty feet wide, and ten feet high.
MSG.2: He made a Sea—an immense round basin of cast metal fifteen feet in diameter, seven and a half feet high, and forty-five feet in circumference.
MSG.3: Just under the rim, there were two parallel bands of something like bulls, ten to each foot and a half. The figures were cast in one piece with the Sea.
MSG.4: The Sea was set on twelve bulls, three facing north, three facing west, three facing south, and three facing east. All the bulls faced outward and supported the Sea on their hindquarters.
MSG.5: The Sea was three inches thick and flared at the rim like a cup, or a lily. It held about 18,000 gallons.
MSG.6: He made ten Washbasins, five set on the right and five on the left, for rinsing the things used for the Whole-Burnt-Offerings. The priests washed themselves in the Sea.
MSG.7: He made ten gold Lampstands, following the specified pattern, and placed five on the right and five on the left.
MSG.8: He made ten tables and set five on the right and five on the left. He also made a hundred gold bowls.
MSG.9: He built a Courtyard especially for the priests and then the great court and doors for the court. The doors were covered with bronze.
MSG.10: He placed the Sea on the right side of The Temple at the southeast corner.
MSG.11:
He also made ash buckets, shovels, and bowls.
And that about wrapped it up: Huram completed the work he had contracted to do for King Solomon:
MSG.12:
two pillars;
two bowl-shaped capitals for the tops of the pillars;
two decorative filigrees for the capitals;
MSG.13: four hundred pomegranates for the filigrees (a double row of pomegranates for each filigree);
MSG.15: one Sea and the twelve bulls under it;
MSG.16:
miscellaneous buckets, forks, shovels, and bowls.
All these artifacts that Huram-Abi made for King Solomon for The Temple of God were made of burnished bronze.
MSG.17: The king had them cast in clay in a foundry on the Jordan plain between Succoth and Zarethan.
MSG.18: These artifacts were never weighed—there were far too many! Nobody has any idea how much bronze was used.
MSG.19:
Solomon was also responsible for the furniture and accessories in The Temple of God:
the gold Altar;
the tables that held the Bread of the Presence;
MSG.20:
the Lampstands of pure gold with their lamps, to be lighted
before the Inner Sanctuary, the Holy of Holies;
MSG.21: the gold flowers, lamps, and tongs (all solid gold);
MSG.22:
the gold wick trimmers, bowls, ladles, and censers;
the gold doors of The Temple, doors to the Holy of Holies, and the doors to the main sanctuary.
